title: A small family spans an essentially small full infinity subcategory
statement: Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U\prime$, local smallness and essential smallness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and quasicategories, equivalences, mapping spaces and full subcategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small quasicategory fitting in $\mathcal U\prime$: each mapping space is equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small space. Let $J$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set and $(X_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of objects of $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal D\subset\mathcal C$ be the full subcategory on all objects equivalent to at least one $X_j$. Then $\mathcal D$ is essentially $\mathcal U$-small: there exist a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $\mathcal D_0$ and an equivalence $\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal D$. The set $J$ is allowed to be empty.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7, implication (1) to (2), and Proposition 5.4.1.2, implication (1) to (3), with Definition 5.4.1.3. Taking the replete closure does not change the equivalence classes or the mapping spaces between chosen representatives. Read online; a reference copy was retained only in the item sandbox for second reading, not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: If $J=\varnothing$, the defining condition on objects of $\mathcal D$ has no witnesses. Thus $\mathcal D$ is the empty simplicial set: every simplex would have a vertex. The empty simplicial set is a small quasicategory, since no inner horn (whose dimension is at least two) maps to it. Take $\mathcal D_0=\mathcal D$ with the identity equivalence. For the rest suppose $J\ne\varnothing$.

The full simplicial subset $\mathcal D$ is a quasicategory. Indeed any inner horn in it has all the vertices of its ambient simplex; an ambient filler in $\mathcal C$ therefore still has all its vertices in $\mathcal D$ and belongs to that full subset. For $x,y\in\mathcal D$, every simplex of the right-pinched mapping space has only $x,y$ as vertices. Consequently $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(x,y)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$ degree by degree. Each is equivalent to a small space by the given local smallness of $\mathcal C$. This verifies the precise mapping-space hypothesis used below, without assuming that the set of actual simplices is small.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7, pass to the full subcategory; mapping-space equality checked from the right-pinched definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-minimal-retract] to the $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory $\mathcal D$. Obtain a minimal quasicategory $M\subseteq\mathcal D$, inclusion $i$, retraction $r$ with $ri=1$, and a coherent natural equivalence $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\simeq ir$. In particular $i$ is a functor equivalence. Neither $M$ nor its simplices have yet been asserted $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Proposition 2.3.3.8 at S equal to a point; the minimal model used in Proposition 5.4.1.2.

proof.text: The function $J\to M_0$, $j\mapsto r(X_j)$, is surjective. For any vertex $m\in M$, the defining replete closure gives an equivalence $i(m)\simeq X_j$ for some $j$. A simplicial functor preserves an equivalence: apply it to the inverse edge and its two inverse-triangle witnesses. Applying $r$ therefore gives an equivalence $m=ri(m)\simeq r(X_j)$ in $M$. For $n=0$ this equivalence edge is exactly a relative-boundary homotopy (the boundary is empty), so minimality gives $m=r(X_j)$. As the image of the small set $J$, the vertex set $M_0$ is in bijection with a small set; repetitions among the $X_j$ do not matter.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.2, induction base n=0, combined with the chosen family in Proposition 5.4.1.7.

proof.text: Induct on $n\geq1$, assuming $M_{n-1}$ is in bijection with a small set. A boundary map $b:\partial\Delta^n\to M$ is determined by its $n+1$ face simplices, subject to face compatibility; hence the set $B_n$ of such maps is a subset of a finite product of copies of $M_{n-1}$ and is also in bijection with a small set. Fix $b\in B_n$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-boundary-extension-small-classes] in $\mathcal D$ to $i b$, using the endpoint mapping-space hypothesis from step 2. Its extension quotient is small. The map sending an extension $f:\Delta^n\to M$ of $b$ to the class of $if$ in that quotient is injective: equality of quotient classes gives a finite chain of relative-boundary homotopies in $\mathcal D$, with directions possibly reversed. Postcompose each homotopy with $r$. Since $ri=1$, each resulting homotopy is constant on $b$ throughout the boundary. Because $n\geq1$, every vertex lies in $\partial\Delta^n$; its track is therefore the degenerate edge at its fixed vertex, which is an equivalence (it is its own inverse, with degenerate inverse triangles). These are exactly the relative-boundary homotopies in the minimality statement, so minimality identifies the two endpoints of every link. The first and last simplices are therefore equal. Thus the set of extensions of $b$ in $M$ is in bijection with a small subset of a small set. Taking the disjoint union over the small set $B_n$ proves that $M_n$ is in bijection with a small set. This is the induction step; an unfillable boundary contributes the empty fibre.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2): induction on simplex dimension, fixed-boundary extension classes, and minimality.

proof.text: For each $n\geq0$ choose a small set $S_n$ and a bijection $e_n:S_n\to M_n$. Transport every simplicial operator $M(\alpha):M_n\to M_m$ to $e_m^{-1}M(\alpha)e_n$. The simplicial identities hold because adjacent $e_ke_k^{-1}$ cancel. These sets and operators define a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $\mathcal D_0$ (there are only countably many degrees and simplex operators), and the $e_n$ form a simplicial isomorphism $e:\mathcal D_0\to M$. For an inner horn $a:\Lambda_k^n\to\mathcal D_0$, compose with $e$, choose a filler $t:\Delta^n\to M$ using the quasicategory property of $M$, and take $e^{-1}t$; its restriction is $e^{-1}ea=a$. Thus $\mathcal D_0$ is a quasicategory. The composite $ie:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal D$ is the required functor equivalence, with inverse $e^{-1}r$; the strict identity $ri=1$ and the coherent natural equivalence from step 3 give its two inverse identities. Thus essential smallness is obtained with an actual small quasicategory, not merely with small equivalence classes of objects.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.2, (2) implies (3), and Definition 5.4.1.3; explicit degreewise transport to the smaller universe.
